stem_book: A particle of mass m is suspended vertically from a vertical line AB at a distance (3√3/8)L from O as shown in figure. The object is given a horizontal velocity u = √(7gL/2). At some point, its motion ceases to be circular and eventually the object passes through the line AB. At the instant of crossing AB, its velocity is horizontal. When the particle's motion ceases to be circular, the angle made by the string with the horizontal is (a) 30° (b) 60° (c) 37° (d) cos⁻¹(2/3)
work: T = m(u²/L − 2g + 3g cosθ) = m(1.5g + 3g cosθ) = 0 ⇒ cosθ = −1/2 ⇒ θ = 120° from bottom ⇒ 30° above horizontal
